# Avatar

Figma: [04c. Avatar](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-913) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-26

User and organization representation in three components. The core Avatar handles a single user with four type options (Photo, Initials, Icon, Placeholder) - falls back gracefully when a photo is missing. AvatarWithStatus adds a Badge Dot overlay for online/offline indicators in chat and presence UIs. AvatarStack handles multi-user contexts like "12 investors committed" or "5 reviewers" with overlapping avatars and a +N counter for overflow. All three respect the design system's shape distinction: Circle for users, Rounded for organizations (developer entities, Safqah itself).

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/avatar/reference.png`

### AvatarWithStatus

Avatar with a Badge Dot overlay showing online, away, busy or offline presence, at sm/md/lg only.

Level: molecule · Contains: Avatar, Badge Dot

Use when:
- Support chat agent who is online now
- Deal-room or chat participants where presence is actionable
- Assigning a back-office reviewer who must be available

Don't use when:
- Past comments or activity feeds where live presence is misleading: use Avatar
- Groups of users: use AvatarStack
- Very small (xs) or hero (xl) avatars: use Avatar and state presence in text

Accessibility: Announce presence in text ("online") alongside the dot; color alone is not enough.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Status | `status` | variant | online, away, busy, offline | online |
| Size | `size` | variant | sm, md, lg | sm |

### AvatarStack

Overlapping group of 2 to 4 avatars with a +N counter for overflow, used to show social proof such as how many investors committed to a deal.

Level: molecule · Contains: Avatar

Use when:
- "12 investors committed" on a deal page, always with a count label beside it
- Reviewers or approvers of a document in back-office
- Collaborators on a shared goal

Don't use when:
- A single person: use Avatar
- The precise number as the main message: use Stat or KeyValue and keep the stack decorative
- A full list of people: use List or ActionList

Accessibility: The stack is decorative; the adjacent label carries the number for screen readers; +N uses Western digits.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Count | `count` | variant | 2, 3, 4, 5+ | 2 |
| Size | `size` | variant | sm, md, lg | sm |

### Avatar

Single user or organization picture with a fallback chain Photo, Initials, Icon, Placeholder. Circle means a person (investor, admin), Rounded means an entity (developer company, bank, Safqah).

Level: atom · Part of: AvatarWithStatus, AvatarStack, ListItem

Use when:
- Investor or support agent in a comment, list row or account header (Shape=Circle)
- Developer company logo on a deal or NewsCard (Shape=Rounded)
- Profile header in settings at Size=xl
- Placeholder while user data loads (Type=Placeholder)

Don't use when:
- Showing online/away presence: use AvatarWithStatus
- Several committed investors: use AvatarStack
- Loading a whole row or card layout: use SkeletonAvatar inside a Skeleton composition
- Brand marks of partners: use SafqahLogo, MadaLogo or AbshirLogo

Accessibility: Photo needs alt text with the person or company name; Initials avatars expose the full name, not the letters.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Type | `type` | variant | Photo, Initials, Icon, Placeholder | Photo |
| Size | `size` | variant | xs, sm, md, lg, xl | xs |
| Shape | `shape` | variant | Circle, Rounded | Circle |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Avatar is the smallest piece of user representation. It appears anywhere Safqah needs to show "who" - comment authors, deal committers, document signatories, reviewers, support agents, account profiles. A complete avatar treatment covers four scenarios: the user has a photo (Photo), the user has no photo but has a name (Initials), the user is anonymous or unloaded (Icon), the data is loading (Placeholder).

AvatarWithStatus extends the core for presence-aware contexts (chat threads, support agents online now, deal-room participants). AvatarStack handles multi-user contexts (committed investors, reviewers, document collaborators) with a defined overlap and overflow counter pattern.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Three components, all built on the core Avatar primitive.

Avatar (core) · 40 variants

Single user representation. 4 types (Photo, Initials, Icon, Placeholder) × 5 sizes (xs, sm, md, lg, xl) × 2 shapes (Circle, Rounded). Photo type uses a gradient placeholder in Figma - the runtime swaps in the actual image fill. Initials show 2 letters with a deterministic color rotation in code (Figma shows the default brand-subtle color).

AvatarWithStatus · 12 variants

4 statuses (online, away, busy, offline) × 3 sizes (sm, md, lg). Wraps the core Avatar with a Badge Dot overlay anchored at the 4-5 o'clock position, with a surface-colored ring around the dot for visual separation. xs and xl skip the status pattern.

AvatarStack · 12 variants

4 counts (2, 3, 4, 5+) × 3 sizes (sm, md, lg). Overlapping group of avatars with rings between each. The 5+ variant shows 4 avatars + a "+N" counter. Default overlap is −8dp at md size. Each instance can have its underlying Avatar swapped to a Photo or specific initials.

### Type taxonomy - fallback hierarchy

The four types are NOT four design choices for the same scenario - they're a fallback hierarchy. Pick Photo if available, then Initials if a name is available, then Icon if only an unknown user identity exists, then Placeholder during data load.

Photo - preferred

When the user has uploaded a profile photo. The avatar is filled with the photo as a circular (or rounded) clip. Figma shows a gradient placeholder with a soft silhouette; runtime swaps in the actual image. Always preferred when available because it's the most personal and recognizable.

Initials - first fallback

When the user has a name but no photo. Show 1-2 character initials (English: first letter of given + family name; Arabic: first letter of first + family name). Background uses a deterministic 8-color rotation based on a hash of the user's name - so the same user always gets the same color across sessions. Default in Figma is brand-primary-subtle.

Icon - second fallback

When neither photo nor name is available (anonymous users, deleted accounts, guest contributors). Shows a generic person glyph on a neutral background. Use sparingly - most users in Safqah have names; if you find yourself reaching for Icon often, the data layer probably needs work.

Placeholder - loading state

Shown while user data is being fetched. Solid skeleton fill, no content. Pairs with shimmer animation at runtime. Once data arrives, the placeholder swaps to one of the other three types based on availability.

### Size - five scales

Five sizes cover the full range of avatar use cases in Safqah, from dense admin tables to profile page heroes. Pick the size based on context and surrounding type scale, not aesthetic preference.

xs

24dp

sm

32dp

md

40dp

lg

56dp

xl

80dp

- xs (24dp) - dense admin tables, contact lists with 8+ rows visible, sidebar nav user pickers
- sm (32dp) - comment threads, search results, recent activity feeds, dropdown user selectors
- md (40dp) - DEFAULT. Deal cards, comment authors, notification senders, account pickers
- lg (56dp) - profile previews in modals, contact detail panels, investor profile cards
- xl (80dp) - profile page hero, account settings page header, large empty states

### Shape - Circle for users, Rounded for organizations

The shape distinction is a semantic signal, not a styling choice. Circle means "this represents a human person". Rounded means "this represents an organization, company, or non-human entity". Picking the wrong shape conveys the wrong relationship.

Circle · users

Investors, developers, admins, agents

Rounded · organizations

Safqah, developer companies, partner entities

> **Info:** For Safqah specifically: investors and developers (as individual humans) get Circle. The Safqah platform itself, real estate development companies, partner banks, and regulatory entities get Rounded. When a developer is a single-person business, use Rounded - the avatar represents the company entity, not the person.

### Initials - 8-color deterministic rotation

When showing initials, the background color is NOT a design choice per instance. It's deterministic: hash the user's name to an index in an 8-color palette, then use that color forever. The same user always gets the same color across sessions, devices, and contexts. Different users get visually distinct colors.

In Figma, the default Initials variant uses brand-primary-subtle (mint green) - this is the visual reference, not the runtime behavior. At runtime, the calling code overrides the fill based on the user hash. The 8 colors below match Safqah's overall palette and ensure adequate contrast on the text in all theme modes.

| AB | CD | EF | GH | IJ | KL | MN | OP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

> **Warning:** NEVER hand-pick a color for an individual initials avatar. The deterministic rotation is what makes a user's avatar recognizable across the product - if Ahmed is mint green on the dashboard but orange on a comment, users won't connect them as the same person. The hash-to-index function lives in code, not in design.

### Hash function for color selection

The runtime selects the color index by hashing the user's name (or user ID for stability across name changes) modulo 8. Implementation: a simple FNV-1a hash on the user.id, then take the lowest 3 bits. This is stable across deploys and gives a roughly uniform distribution.

### AvatarWithStatus - presence pattern

Online/offline indicators are anchored at the 4-5 o'clock position with a surface-colored ring around the dot. The ring is crucial - it visually separates the dot from the avatar so the dot reads as "on top of" the avatar rather than "part of" it.

Online · success

Active in last 5 min

Away · warning

Idle 5-30 min

Busy · error

Do not disturb (manually set)

Offline · neutral

No activity for 30+ min

- Status reuses Badge Dot (04b) - same tones (success, warning, error, neutral), same sizes. The status pattern is just Avatar + Badge Dot + ring, no new colors.
- The ring is bg/surface - when the avatar sits on a card with a different background, the ring blends with the card. This makes the dot read as floating above the surface rather than touching the avatar edge.
- xs (24dp) and xl (80dp) skip the status pattern. xs is too small (dot would compete with the avatar). xl rarely appears in contexts that need status (profile heroes don't need online indicators).

### AvatarStack - overflow pattern

When a context has multiple users (committed investors, reviewers, document collaborators), use AvatarStack with overlapping avatars and a "+N" counter for overflow. The default shows up to 4 avatars + counter; lists with fewer users use the 2/3/4 variants.

Count = 2

Count = 3

Count = 4

Count = 5+

- Overlap is −8dp at md size, scaled proportionally for sm and lg. Each avatar gets a surface-colored ring matching the AvatarWithStatus pattern.
- The "+N" counter on the 5+ variant uses bg/disabled background with text/default. Default text is "+8" - override per instance to match the actual overflow count.
- Pair the stack with a label nearby: "12 investors committed", "5 reviewers approved". The stack alone is a visual anchor; the count is in the label, not in the user's head.

### Code examples

How to consume the Avatar family in Flutter.

### Flutter - Avatar with fallback hierarchy

```dart
// SafqahAvatar handles the fallback hierarchy automatically:
// 1. Photo if photoUrl is non-null AND loads successfully
// 2. Initials if user.fullName is non-null
// 3. Icon if neither (anonymous / deleted user)
// 4. Placeholder while data is loading

SafqahAvatar(
  user: deal.investor,
  size: AvatarSize.md,
  shape: AvatarShape.circle,
)

// Override the type explicitly if needed (rare)
SafqahAvatar(
  user: deal.investor,
  size: AvatarSize.md,
  shape: AvatarShape.circle,
  forceType: AvatarType.initials,  // skip photo even if available
)
```

### Flutter - Initials color rotation

```dart
// The 8-color rotation palette - must match the doc page
const INITIALS_ROTATION = [
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFD6F2DF, text: 0xFF0F6B3C),  // emerald
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFEBF2FF, text: 0xFF2952CC),  // blue
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFFFF3D6, text: 0xFF995200),  // amber
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFF0E8F7, text: 0xFF5A2E94),  // violet
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFE0F5F7, text: 0xFF0E6B7A),  // cyan
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFFFEAD1, text: 0xFFA14000),  // orange
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFD6F0EE, text: 0xFF0A6B66),  // teal
  AvatarColor(bg: 0xFFFCE0E0, text: 0xFFA30013),  // red
];

// Hash function - deterministic, stable across deploys
int colorIndexForUser(String userId) {
  // FNV-1a hash
  int hash = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (final c in userId.codeUnits) {
    hash = (hash ^ c) * 0x01000193 & 0xFFFFFFFF;
  }
  return hash & 0x07;  // mod 8
}

AvatarColor colorForUser(User user) {
  // Use user.id for stability - name can change, ID can't
  return INITIALS_ROTATION[colorIndexForUser(user.id)];
}
```

### Flutter - AvatarWithStatus

```dart
// Status comes from presence service, not user data
SafqahAvatarWithStatus(
  user: deal.investor,
  status: presenceService.statusFor(deal.investor.id),
  size: AvatarSize.md,
)

// In a chat thread header
Row(
  children: [
    SafqahAvatarWithStatus(
      user: thread.otherParticipant,
      status: presenceService.statusFor(thread.otherParticipant.id),
      size: AvatarSize.sm,
    ),
    SizedBox(width: 12),
    Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
      children: [
        Text(thread.otherParticipant.displayName),
        Text(statusDisplayLabel(status), style: muted),
      ],
    ),
  ],
)
```

### Flutter - AvatarStack with overflow

```dart
// Show up to 4 avatars, then +N for the rest
SafqahAvatarStack(
  users: deal.committedInvestors,  // List<User>
  maxVisible: 4,
  size: AvatarSize.md,
)

// In a deal card with label
Row(
  children: [
    SafqahAvatarStack(
      users: deal.committedInvestors,
      maxVisible: 4,
      size: AvatarSize.sm,
    ),
    SizedBox(width: 12),
    Text(
      i18n.t('deal.committed_by_count', count: deal.committedInvestors.length),
      // "12 investors committed" / "ساهم 12 مستثمر"
    ),
  ],
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four scenarios specific to avatar choice and composition.

- **Do** · Investor profile in a deal card: Use Circle shape - investors are human users. Use Photo if available, otherwise the runtime falls back to Initials → Icon → Placeholder. Size md is the default for deal cards.
- **Don't** · Investor profile in a deal card: Don't use Rounded shape for individual users. Rounded means "organization, company, entity". Mixing shapes across user types breaks the semantic signal users learn from the rest of the product.
- **Do** · Developer company logo on a deal: Use Rounded shape - developer is a company entity. Use Initials with the company's first letter (or its 2-letter code) on the brand color. Default size lg works for deal headers.
- **Don't** · Developer company logo on a deal: Don't use Circle for an organization. Even if the developer is a single-person business, the avatar represents the company entity, not the person - Circle would suggest the deal is with the individual.
- **Do** · List of committed investors: Use AvatarStack with the 5+ variant + a label "X investors committed". The stack provides a visual anchor; the label provides the precise count and screen-reader-readable text.
- **Don't** · List of committed investors: Don't use a regular list of separate avatars for >3 users - takes too much horizontal space. Don't use a stack alone without a count label - users have to estimate the number. Don't hand-roll the overlap; the spacing is calibrated for visual rhythm.
- **Do** · Chat thread with online status: Use AvatarWithStatus when presence is relevant (chat, support agent assignment, deal-room participants). The dot is anchored at the 4-5 o'clock position with a surface-colored ring. Status comes from the presence service.
- **Don't** · Chat thread with online status: Don't add a status dot to contexts where presence isn't actionable (e.g., past comment authors, historical activity feeds). Showing "online now" on a comment from 3 days ago is misleading - the user wasn't online when they posted.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and rules to live by.

> **Warning:** The 8-color rotation palette is documented in 04c (this page) and must match the Flutter constant `INITIALS_ROTATION` exactly. If you change a color in one place, change it in both. The runtime test should snapshot the rotation against the doc page swatches.

> **Info:** Photo type in Figma uses a teal-to-violet gradient + white silhouette as a placeholder. This is design-time only - runtime swaps in the actual image fill via Flutter's Image widget. Don't treat the gradient as a brand color; it has no semantic meaning.

> **Info:** AvatarWithStatus reuses the Badge Dot component from 04b - there's no separate "status dot for avatars" component. If you ever need a status color that's not already in Badge Dot, add it there first, not here.

> **Info:** The ring color is bg/surface, NOT bg/base or bg/elevated. This is intentional - the ring should blend with the OUTERMOST surface (the page background). When an avatar is on a card (bg/base), the ring stands out against the card. When the avatar is on the page (bg/surface), the ring is invisible - but that's fine, because there's no avatar adjacent to it to separate.

> **Info:** Initials should ALWAYS be 1-2 characters. In English, take the first letter of first + last name. In Arabic, take the first letter of first + last name (Arabic letters are wider, so 2 characters may need a smaller font). For names with one word ("Ahmed"), use the first letter only ("A"). The text rendering handles this - the component shows whatever string is passed.

> **Warning:** Stack overlap is a NEGATIVE itemSpacing - at md size, items overlap by 8dp. This means the visible width of a 4-avatar stack is NOT 4 × 40 = 160dp; it's ~136dp. Plan layout space accordingly when fitting a stack into a row.

> **Info:** The +N counter in the 5+ stack variant uses bg/disabled. This is intentional - the counter is NOT a user, so it shouldn't use a personal-color (no rotation palette). The neutral gray reads as "more" affordance rather than "person".

> **Warning:** xs (24dp) does NOT have a status pattern. The dot at 24dp would be 4-5dp, which is too small for a meaningful color cue and visually competes with the avatar. If you need presence indication at xs, render the status separately as a colored text label ("· online").

> **Info:** For organizations (Rounded shape) with no logo, use the company's first 1-2 letters as Initials. "Safqah Capital" → "SC", "ABC Real Estate" → "ABC" or "AB" depending on size. The color rotation works for organizations too - just hash the company name/ID.

> **Warning:** Auto-layout caveat - AvatarWithStatus uses NONE layout (manual positioning) because the dot+ring overlap the avatar and would break auto-layout sizing. Instances can't be put inside a HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL parent that's set to HUG - wrap them in a fixed-size frame or pad the parent to accommodate the overflow.
